selection_note: Explicit upstream upgrade batch 10, schema v2 unrestricted across included Index (all S1–S5). Public read-only discovery from Index 3896a2de54399beb137f9e9959bb2587ebf4fc4a and Upstream ac0f154cc7d35622ec1b981efe0752b35db167f3 found 830 available and 10 source-disjoint assessments; feature-first preregistration was published BEFORE target source/issue inspection at 911456fc4acca4df5b9f38eac1395e97c3355aec. All ten originals screened from exact public default SHAs. Five CLOSED_NO_CHANGE, five BLOCKED_EVIDENCE; no admitted patches, native matched RED/GREEN, independent runner, external PR or VSM regrade. Index main later advanced to descendant 75bb11f; original frozen assessment pin preserved. Read-only snapshot is not atomic source reservation. Controller NO_ACTIONABLE_CANDIDATE.

candidates.finding: Could an opt-in observation/action receipt diagnostic improve the single-episode hand-in?
candidates.screening_result: License-first source-screen: root MIT; First-party PostToolUse hook already correlates native observation identifiers, verifies immutable receipt SHA/images, tracks delayed background gaps and supplies repeated-capture diagnostics. Incremental missing operator workflow and native benefit were not established; the single-episode S1 assessment does not imply missing S2.

candidates.finding: Would a non-mutating worker-capacity/ticket-impact preview help an operator before changing maxWorkers?
candidates.screening_result: License-first source-screen: root MIT; First-party operator overview exposes open tickets, idle count, executor running load and maxWorkers; settings use validated optimistic-concurrency saves. A new hypothetical capacity-impact model lacks first-party demand, frozen expected behavior and independently executable before/after acceptance.
candidates.blocker: Need and counterfactual for a new prediction workflow are not source-verified; no native test/independent runner.

candidates.finding: Would an opt-in framework evaluation baseline/candidate comparison before adoption improve the evolution workflow?
candidates.screening_result: License-first source-screen: root Apache-2.0; First-party Platform already freezes a Candidate, requires human selection for experiment, submits independent Benchmark evaluation and consumes verdicts. A distinct user-needed comparison/report path beyond the current verdict has not been established with a concrete accepted scenario.
candidates.blocker: No first-party requested comparison output or matched native baseline; no permission to assert improved framework outcomes.

candidates.finding: Would a per-subject queued/claimed suppression-reason view improve collision triage?
candidates.screening_result: License-first source-screen: root MIT; The kernel already records subject/lane, queued and claimed states, and per-run event history; its supported CLI explicitly offers `status`, `runs` and `why <round>` to explain a run. No independent new scenario unavailable from these current inspection surfaces was shown.

candidates.finding: Would a separate review-coverage/unresolved-finding pre-delivery matrix help supervisor closure?
candidates.screening_result: License-first source-screen: root MIT; First-party independent Codex reviewer already checks actual diff and criteria, emits PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN conditions and a bounded full report via `OutFile`; supervisor policy consumes review findings. No distinct required matrix or independently supported benefit was evidenced. Native Windows PowerShell reviewer/model was not executed.

candidates.finding: Would a non-mutating file-scope collision preview before fanout improve cross-wave decisions?
candidates.screening_result: License-first source-screen: root MIT with NOTICE; The shipped `/fanout` plan already marks parallel versus `after` dependencies and instructs the orchestrator to serialize uncertain or overlapping file/package scopes, then reconcile sibling branches. A separate deterministic preflight beyond this orchestration requires demonstrated first-party need, stable scope input and native acceptance. Root LICENSE grants MIT; NOTICE identifies separately licensed copied components outside this proposed path.
candidates.blocker: No independently established missing preflight, counterfactual or native executable first-party input contract.

candidates.finding: Would an offline tool/permission pre-task explanation improve local task readiness?
candidates.screening_result: License-first source-screen: root MIT; The first-party S1 loop rejects provider profiles with `supportsTools !== true` before task model actions and returns normalized tool execution errors. An additional offline user-facing pre-task inventory has not been tied to an actual reported missing tool scenario or bounded CLI contract.
candidates.blocker: Need for separate preflight over existing capability guard and tool errors unverified; no native matched test.

candidates.finding: Would additional read-only rerun discrepancy classification improve independent report triage?
candidates.screening_result: License-first source-screen: root MIT-0; Current original main advanced to 41c2360e10259c09af12b5845af3e7d573d07ae2 after assessed review. Its first-party protocol already records clean checkout, per-step outputs, parser-recognized test counts, timeout attribution, NOT RUN and NEEDS service explanations, without converting tests into overall task success. New distinct discrepancy classification lacks an evidenced native case; no reruns performed.

candidates.finding: Would operator-facing session/tool denial-reason preview improve current RBAC intervention?
candidates.screening_result: License-first source-screen: root Apache-2.0; Current main advanced to 24b0170028ae7683867d2b8d5ce1589d8ace12eb. The current authenticated `/api/rbac/me` exposes effective roles, admin state and sorted accessible tools, and role APIs already modify allocations. Whether a separate reason-before-denial preview improves an actual supported session/tool path remains unverified.
candidates.blocker: Need and strict counterfactual for a second preview beyond effective entitlement API not established; no native matched test.

candidates.finding: Would a separate read-only grouped browser verification failure summary improve targeted rework?
candidates.screening_result: License-first source-screen: root MIT; The optional first-party tester recipe already requires user-flow steps, console/network failures and a final `works`/`fix first`/`could not test` verdict with reasons. `beforeStop` hook returns feedback or one-time note into correction/completion. A separate failure aggregation has no independently evidenced increment. No browser or model runs executed.
